text:
**Short answer:** it depends on whether you need to run a roof A/C. The sources don't point to one best combo, so here are three tiers.

## 1. Weekend trips, no A/C (budget combo)
**ALLPOWERS P1800 (1,024Wh) + SP037 400W folding panel kit**
- $731, or $657.90 with code ALLPOWERS26 (tested in the store's cart on 2026-10-25).
- Buy: https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-p1800-sp037-solar-kit
- This is an affiliate link, so Dealectric earns a commission at no cost to you. Only the retailer's page covers this brand, and the independent comparison sites don't review it. I also couldn't confirm the P1800's maximum solar input, so check that it can take the full 400W before you buy.

**Step up:** ALLPOWERS S2000 Pro (1,451Wh) + SP037 400W kit, $963, or $866.70 with the same code.
- Buy: https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-s2000-pro-sp037-solar-kit

## 2. Mid-size RV, fridge, electronics, some boondocking
**BLUETTI AC200L (2,048Wh, 2,400W, up to 1,200W solar input)**
- The RV-power-station roundup calls it the budget pick with a built-in 30A RV outlet (https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/).
- The camping guide lists its max solar input at 1,200W, which is the highest solar ceiling among the 2,000Wh-class units in that list (https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/).
- It weighs about 62 lb.
- The roundup lists it with an Amazon link but I don't have a direct product URL. Pair it with 400W or more of folding panels.

## 3. Full-time or running A/C off-grid
**EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 (4,096Wh, 4,000W continuous, 8,000W surge)**
- The roundup ranks it best overall for RVs. It can expand past 12kWh and recharges 0–80% in about 50 minutes from a wall outlet (https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/).
- A 13,500 BTU roof A/C draws about 1,500W running but spikes past 3,000W at startup, so you need a unit with surge headroom like this one.
- It's heavy, a two-person lift, and the most expensive option once you add batteries.
- Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro (3,024Wh, 3,000W) is the simpler alternative, per the same roundup.

## Things to check before buying
- **Solar input ceiling:** a big array is wasted if the station caps input. The camping guide lists the Jackery 2000 v2 and 1000 v2 at just 400W, versus 1,000W for the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus.
- **Pricing conflicts:** the sources disagree on some prices and specs, and they are affiliate-driven. Confirm specs and price on the manufacturer's page.
- **Hardwiring:** connecting a station to your RV's electrical system may need a licensed electrician.

If you tell me what you want to run (A/C, fridge, Starlink, CPAP), how many nights off-grid, and your budget, I can narrow this to one pick.
